title: Exec brief and OKR alignment playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for the upcoming company-wide town + exec briefing cycle. It stitches together: a concise executive briefing slide narrative, a suggested set of company-level OKR drafts for leadership alignment, the all-hands agenda and asks, plus rehearsal/runbook items so the event is smooth and the messaging is consistent across teams.

Audience:
- CEO/CXO/Executives (final alignment)
- People managers and IC leads (context for all-hands)
- Product/Eng/GTM leads (input on OKR targets and signals)

High-level timeline (target dates):
- Feb 14: initial draft circulated (this file)
- Feb 21: leadership review / consolidation of comments
- Feb 25: slides locked for exec briefing; OKRs in first pass (owners assigned)
- Mar 3: all-hands dry run (leadership + comms)
- Mar 6: company all-hands (public)

Key objectives for the cadence:
1) Clarity: single narrative about where Redwood is headed this year (customer problems, product bets, operational priorities).
2) Alignment: leadership signs off on company-level OKRs and endorses measurement signals.
3) Motivation: all-hands content should celebrate wins, call out persistent challenges, and explain how individual teams contribute.
4) Actionability: each company OKR must have 1–2 named owners and 3 leading indicators.

Draft company-level OKRs (working):
- Objective A: Make inference predictable and cost-efficient for production users
  - KR1: Reduce median token cost-per-request by 20% on hosted API (baseline: Oct 2024)
  - KR2: Increase percent of customer traffic using caching/batching recommendations to 40%
  - KR3: Ship automated quantization recommendation flow in Redwood Optimize and get 10 paying customers on it
  - Owners: eng-serving-runtime (Liam C.), product-optimize (Maya P.)

- Objective B: Win enterprise adoption for Dedicated & Private offerings
  - KR1: Close 6 Dedicated contracts >$100k ARR
  - KR2: Complete SOC2 + 2 region private-deployments reference installs
  - KR3: Reduce deployment onboarding time for Private from 30d to 12d
  - Owners: sales-enterprise, eng-private-delivery (Diego R.)

- Objective C: Deliver world-class reliability and observability for customer-facing production workloads
  - KR1: Meeting latency SLOs (p95 < target) for 95% of production routes
  - KR2: Implement token-level tracing in Console for top 5 customers
  - KR3: Reduce incident-to-closure mean time by 30%
  - Owners: site-reliability-engineering (SRE lead), observability team

Notes on KR design (working):
- Each KR needs a primary metric, one or two leading indicators, and a triage/escalation path if on-track fails.
- Avoid mixing output metrics (revenue) with engineering readiness metrics; separate them into company-level vs supporting OKRs.

Executive briefing narrative (slide-by-slide sketch):
1) One-line state: where Redwood is (momentum + main constraint)
2) Market context: open model landscape + why serving wins; competitive map (1 slide)
3) Key metrics snapshot: ARR growth, committed capacity, latency SLOs, avg token unit economics
4) Product bets and milestones this year: Hosted API improvements, Dedicated commits, Private deployment program, Optimize roadmap
5) Company OKRs (3–4 slides): objectives + 1–2 KRs per objective, owners, current baseline & timeline
6) Risks & mitigations: supply constraints, hiring velocity, model regression risk
7) Asks of organization: concrete levers teams can pull this quarter
8) All-hands agenda + close: how managers should follow up with teams

All-hands agenda (60 minutes recommended):
- 0–5m: Welcome + one-line state (CEO)
- 5–15m: Product demo: new Optimize flow or hosted latency improvements (PM + Eng)
- 15–25m: Customer highlight / case study (Solutions Eng + customer clip)
- 25–35m: OKR walk-through and what it means for each org (COO/VPs)
- 35–45m: Live Q&A (moderated)
- 45–55m: Recognition + shoutouts + hires update
- 55–60m: Wrap + next steps + manager playbook (what to do in team meetings)

Communication and post-all-hands follow-up plan:
- Day 0 (immediately after): Slides + one-page summary posted to Confluence; short TL;DR announcement in #company-feed
- Day 1–3: Manager kit sent with suggested talking points and small group exercise to align squad OKRs to company OKRs
- Week 2: OKR intake window closes; teams must nominate supporting KRs and owners for review

Manager kit (bullet checklist):
- Read the one-pager + slide deck
- Schedule 30–45m team sync to translate company OKRs into team-level commitments
- Capture 3 supporting KRs with owners and leading indicators
- Submit to OKR intake spreadsheet (link in linked artifacts)

Runbook for dry run and live event (technical & comms):
- 3 days out: rehearsal with all presenters; confirm slide transitions and live demo fallbacks
- 1 day out: AV check in each conference room + remote streaming test
- 2 hours before: comms posts scheduled; remind managers
- On event: MC (People Ops) logs audience questions into a shared Google Sheet for response tracking
- Post event: close loop on unanswered questions within 3 business days

Open questions (items for leadership discussion):
- Do we want to tie any compensation or promotion cycles to company-level OKRs this quarter? (pros/cons)
- Which of the proposed KRs should be escalated into sales quota metrics vs product success metrics?
- Are the baseline numbers for KR1 (cost reduction) accurate? Need analytics owner to confirm.

Action items (assigned):
- Aisha: consolidate feedback by Feb 21; produce slide deck skeleton by Feb 25
- Liam: validate token cost baseline + propose two levers for >10% reduction by end of Q2
- Maya: draft Optimize recommendation flow plan and customer beta list by Feb 21
- Diego: confirm Private deployment references and update onboarding time baseline

Appendix (attachments to prepare):
- Metrics snapshot export (product analytics + billing)
- Customer success top-10 deck (short blurbs)
- Draft manager kit doc and intake spreadsheet

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Keep language simple for all-hands; cut technical depth in the main talk, use breakout docs for detail
- Need a short 90s customer video—ask Solutions Eng for options
- Consider a follow-up AMA with CTO focused on quantization & inference optimizations
- TODO: confirm AV vendor for larger space, budget approval required (OPS-890).

End of draft.

Feedback request: please comment inline in this doc, tag owners with direct suggestions, and flag any KRs that look unmeasurable or unowned.
